item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I see a fair amount of dislike for the exploding feature, and SsnakeBite pointed out back in 2014 that one going off is likely to kill the rest of the swarm. But has no one noticed the potential for a chain reaction?

They don't like bright lights and loud noises; such as you get when 20 pounds of C4 goes off. Think of how many thousand microscopic crabs would be needed to replicate something the size of a chair. Folks think 9.07 kg of explosive is OP? Try 9.07x10X, for X of a million or more.

Eh… why not:

While SCP-236 has not been observed to frequently mimic organic life, the possibility exists for SCP-236 to develop this behavior. Notably, during testing with SCP-2366…

item.title: Re: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
I know this is old, but I think this paragraph in particular still needs to be edited. It explicitly states that SCP-236 has not been observed to mimic organic life, then describes a test in which it did. I am disappointed that no one caught this when the edit was made.

I suggest that the beginning of this paragraph be changed to something like:

SCP-236 has only been observed to mimic organic life on X occasions during testing. If this behavior were to become frequent, the danger associated with SCP-236 would be increased considerably. Notably…

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I've also noted something. At the beginning, it states that one unit can consume an object and then lay an egg, which will hatch in 10 minutes or so.

In another point, it states that, and here i quote, "Moderate size swarms can convert a whole human being in less than five minutes".

Perhaps I'm seeing this by the wrong side, but how is it possible to fully convert something (i.e. detaching it, eating it, lay an egg and wait for it to hatch) all in five minutes if the hatching alone takes ten?

item.title: Re: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
That's a good point.

Perhaps something like:

While SCP-236 has not been observed to mimic organic life, the possibility exists for SCP-236 to develop this behavior. Notably, during testing with SCP-2366 when SCP-236 mimicked a brown bear and began to exhibit increased predatory behavior and [DATA EXPUNGED]. Such formations are to be immediately reported, and testing area cleared immediately.

item.title: Re: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded: Good conceptually, but "Notably, during testing with SCP-2366" should be expanded to a complete thought — what did it mimic, and what went wrong that makes it an emergency now? The latter can stay a [DATA EXPUNGED] for all I care, but it should be addressed.

For this article, I'd like to propose a link to SCP-2366. This is due to the latter's effect on organisms and the promotion of cooperative behavior. SCP-236 already does this on its own accord, however the addendum hints that when it was exposed to "something" the swarm was able to mimic organic life, which is what SCP-2366 primarily effects. Additionally, given how SCP-236 is able to construct new instances of itself out of organic material, which is again, something that SCP-2366 effects, I think having SCP-2366 as the "something" that caused the swarm to behave like "organic organisms" would make sense.

Editing this passage:

While SCP-236 has not been observed to mimic organic life, the possibility exists for SCP-236 to develop this behavior. Notably, during testing on [DATA EXPUNGED]. Such formations are to be immediately reported, and testing area cleared immediately.

To read:

While SCP-236 has not been observed to mimic organic life, the possibility exists for SCP-236 to develop this behavior. Notably, during testing with SCP-2366. Such formations are to be immediately reported, and testing area cleared immediately.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.content:encoded: A microscopic, organic being blowing up as hard as 20 pounds of C-4? I mean, even though this site is for impossible things, this seems a bit too far-fetched for me. Maybe if the whole swarm would do this, sure, obviously. And might be you meant that, but I misread it. But not single beings, IMHO.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
When I first started reading this, I was hoping it was going to exploit the inherent creepiness of "any given piece of furniture you sit down on might in fact be made of tiny crabs" — the mental image of them swarming all over me was horrifying.

But then "they blow up" feels like a very clumsy twist, and as many other commenters have pointed out, the size of the explosion is just silly.

I feel like this would work a lot better if the explosion bit were removed altogether, and the "crabs swarm and eat humans" part were explicitly said to be as a result of people sitting / lying on furniture made of crabs. Better still if the crabs are such amazing mimics that people don't even notice at first, only getting eaten after they fall asleep… I realize that this is one possible interpretation of what is already written, but I feel like this is an instance where it shouldn't just be left unsaid. Make me afraid of sitting on a chair made of crabs!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Heh, it's alright but nothing special and the final paragraph (before the addendum) seems to be trying way too hard to be creepy, what with the whole "it's crawling up inside you while you sleep!" and "it eats you inside out!" things.

And as others pointed out, one individual exploding with the force of 9.07 kilos of C4 (by the way, seems like I'm spotting a direct pounds-to-kilos translation here) seems rather silly, not to mention counter-productive as a defence mechanism. I can understand one individual sacrificing itself for the group, but do you have any idea how big an explosion 9 bloody kilos of C4 will create?! There's no way the swarm is surviving this.

Finally, I agree with FortuneFavorsBold that the expungement at the end is completely unnecessary and actually counter-productive.
